syllabus.note: UP Board Biology Class 12 — 13 chapters, 5 units.

books.book_name: NCERT Biology Part I & Part II
books.note: UP Board syllabus fully based on NCERT.

chapters.name: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants
topics: Flower structure — calyx, corolla, androecium, gynoecium, thalamus
Male gametophyte — microsporogenesis, pollen grain structure (exine/intine)
Female gametophyte — megasporogenesis, development of embryo sac (7-celled, 8-nucleate)
Pollination — types: self-pollination (autogamy, geitonogamy), cross-pollination (xenogamy)
Agencies of pollination: wind (anemophily), water (hydrophily), insects (entomophily)
Outbreeding devices, pollen-pistil interaction
Double fertilisation — syngamy (egg + male gamete → zygote) + triple fusion (2 polar nuclei + male gamete → endosperm)
Post-fertilisation events — development of endosperm, embryo, seed, fruit
Apomixis, parthenocarpy, polyembryony
Significance of seed dispersal and fruit formation

chapters.name: Human Reproduction
topics: Male reproductive system — testis (seminiferous tubules, Leydig cells, Sertoli cells), epididymis, vas deferens, prostate, seminal vesicles, urethra
Spermatogenesis — process of sperm formation in testis
Structure of sperm — head (acrosome, nucleus), middle piece (mitochondria), tail (flagellum)
Female reproductive system — ovaries, fallopian tubes, uterus, cervix, vagina
Oogenesis — formation of ovum
Menstrual cycle — follicular phase, ovulation, luteal phase (approx 28 days)
Fertilisation — in fallopian tube, formation of zygote
Embryo development — morula, blastocyst, implantation
Placenta — functions (nutrition, excretion, hormone production)
Parturition (birth), lactation

chapters.name: Reproductive Health
topics: Need for reproductive health — STDs (Sexually Transmitted Diseases)
Birth control — need and methods: barrier (condom, diaphragm), IUDs, oral contraceptives, surgical (vasectomy, tubectomy)
Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) — legal and ethical issues
Amniocentesis — prenatal diagnosis, legal restrictions
Infertility — causes and assisted reproductive technologies
ART: IVF (In Vitro Fertilisation), ZIFT (Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer), GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer)
IUI (Intra Uterine Insemination)

chapters.name: Principles of Inheritance and Variation
topics: Mendel's laws — Law of Dominance, Law of Segregation, Law of Independent Assortment
Monohybrid cross — F1 and F2 ratios (3:1 phenotypic, 1:2:1 genotypic)
Dihybrid cross — 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio using checker board
Test cross and back cross
Incomplete dominance (e.g. snapdragon — pink F1)
Co-dominance (e.g. ABO blood groups)
Multiple allelism — ABO blood groups (IA, IB, i alleles)
Pleiotropy
Chromosomal theory of inheritance — Morgan's experiments on Drosophila
Linkage and crossing over
Sex determination — XY in humans, ZW in birds, XO in grasshopper, haplo-diploid in honeybees
Mutation — point mutation, chromosomal aberration
Sex-linked inheritance — haemophilia, colour blindness
Mendelian disorders — thalassaemia
Chromosomal disorders — Down's syndrome (trisomy 21), Turner's syndrome (45 X0), Klinefelter's syndrome (47 XXY)
chapters.note: Unit: Genetics and Evolution | Difficulty: Medium-Hard

chapters.name: Molecular Basis of Inheritance
topics: DNA as genetic material — Griffith's experiment, Hershey-Chase experiment
Structure of DNA — Watson and Crick double helix model
DNA packaging — nucleosome structure
DNA replication — semi-conservative model, enzymes involved
Transcription in prokaryotes — RNA polymerase, template strand, coding strand
Types of RNA — mRNA, tRNA, rRNA
Translation — ribosomes, codons, anticodons, polysomes
Genetic code — characteristics (triplet, degenerate, universal, non-overlapping)
Gene expression and regulation — lac operon (E. coli)
Genome and Human Genome Project (HGP)
DNA fingerprinting
chapters.note: Unit: Genetics and Evolution | Difficulty: Medium-Hard

chapters.name: Evolution
topics: Origin of life — Oparin and Haldane hypothesis, Miller and Urey experiment
Evidences for biological evolution — palaeontology, comparative anatomy (homologous and analogous organs), embryology, molecular evidence
Darwin's theory — natural selection, survival of the fittest
Hardy-Weinberg principle — gene pool, gene frequency
Mechanisms of evolution — mutation, natural selection, genetic drift, gene flow
Adaptive radiation
Types of natural selection — stabilising, directional, disruptive
Human evolution — Australopithecines, Homo habilis, Homo erectus, Homo sapiens
chapters.note: Unit: Genetics and Evolution | Difficulty: Medium

chapters.name: Human Health and Diseases
topics: Pathogens causing human diseases
Malaria — Plasmodium, life cycle, Anopheles mosquito vector
Dengue — Aedes mosquito, break-bone fever
Typhoid — Salmonella typhi, Widal test
Pneumonia — Streptococcus pneumoniae
Common cold — rhinovirus
Amoebiasis — Entamoeba histolytica
Filariasis — Wuchereria bancrofti
Ascariasis — Ascaris lumbricoides
Ringworm — Microsporum, Trichophyton
Immunology — innate and acquired immunity, antibodies, lymphocytes (B and T cells)
Vaccines — active and passive immunisation, types of vaccines
Cancer — types, causes, treatment
HIV/AIDS — transmission, symptoms, ELISA test
Drug and alcohol abuse — effects on body
chapters.note: Unit: Biology and Human Welfare | Difficulty: Easy-Medium

chapters.name: Microbes in Human Welfare
topics: Microbes in food processing — Lactobacillus in curd, baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) in bread, fermented beverages
Industrial products — antibiotics (Penicillin from Penicillium notatum), enzymes, organic acids, vitamins
Microbes in sewage treatment — primary and secondary treatment, BOD
Microbes in energy generation — biogas (methanogens), biogas plant
Biocontrol agents — Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt), NPV (Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus)
Biofertilisers — Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azospirillum, mycorrhiza, Anabaena
chapters.note: Unit: Biology and Human Welfare | Difficulty: Easy-Medium

chapters.name: Biotechnology — Principles and Processes
topics: Genetic engineering — recombinant DNA technology (rDNA technology)
Restriction enzymes (endonucleases) — type I, II, III; functions, examples (EcoRI, BamHI)
Cloning vectors — plasmids, bacteriophage, cosmids; characteristics of cloning vectors
Gel electrophoresis — separation of DNA fragments
PCR — Polymerase Chain Reaction; Taq polymerase
Transformation — introducing recombinant DNA into host cell
Tools of genetic engineering: restriction enzymes, ligases, polymerases
chapters.note: Unit: Biotechnology and its Applications | Difficulty: Medium

chapters.name: Biotechnology and Its Applications
topics: Biotechnology in health — human insulin production (Humulin), vaccines, gene therapy
Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs) — Bt crops (Bt cotton, Bt brinjal, Bt maize)
Bt toxin — Cry proteins from Bacillus thuringiensis
Transgenic animals — mice, cows; uses in medicine and research
Gene therapy — ADA deficiency example
Biopiracy and biosafety issues
Golden rice, Flavr Savr tomato
rDNA technology applications in medicine
Human Genome Project (HGP) — goals, features
chapters.note: Unit: Biotechnology and its Applications | Difficulty: Medium

chapters.name: Organisms and Population
topics: Ecology — levels of organisation: organism, population, community, ecosystem, biome, biosphere
Population attributes — birth rate, death rate, age distribution, sex ratio
Population growth models — exponential growth (J-shaped curve: dN/dt = rN) and logistic growth (S-shaped curve: dN/dt = rN(K-N)/K)
Population interactions: mutualism, competition, predation, parasitism, commensalism, amensalism
Competitive exclusion principle (Gause's principle)
Adaptations of organisms to environment
chapters.note: Unit: Ecology and Environment | Difficulty: Medium

chapters.name: Ecosystem
topics: Ecosystem — structure and function: biotic and abiotic components
Producers, consumers, decomposers
Food chain and food web
Energy flow — 10% law (Lindeman's law), energy pyramids
Ecological pyramids — pyramid of number, biomass, energy
Productivity — gross and net primary productivity
Decomposition — steps: fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification, mineralisation
Nutrient cycling — carbon cycle, phosphorus cycle
Ecosystem services
chapters.note: Unit: Ecology and Environment | Difficulty: Medium

chapters.name: Biodiversity and Its Conservation
topics: Biodiversity — concept, levels: genetic, species, ecosystem diversity
Patterns of biodiversity — latitudinal gradients, species-area relationship
Importance of biodiversity — ecosystem services
Loss of biodiversity — causes: habitat loss, overexploitation, alien species, co-extinction
Biodiversity conservation — in situ (national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, biosphere reserves, sacred groves) and ex situ (zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks)
Hotspots — Eastern Himalayas, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma, Sri Lanka
Endangered organisms, Red Data Book, IUCN
chapters.note: Unit: Ecology and Environment | Difficulty: Easy-Medium

important_formula_sheets.note: Key formulas / laws for population ecology, energy flow, genetics, molecular biology.

formulas: Logistic growth: dN/dt = rN(K-N)/K  (S-shaped curve, K = carrying capacity)
Birth rate = number of births per capita per unit time
Death rate = number of deaths per capita per unit time
10% Law (Lindeman): only 10% of energy is transferred from one trophic level to next
GPP (Gross Primary Productivity) = total rate of photosynthesis
NPP (Net Primary Productivity) = GPP - Respiration losses
Test cross = F1 hybrid x homozygous recessive parent
Complementary base pairs in DNA: A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3 H-bonds)
Nucleotide = Sugar + Nitrogenous base + Phosphate group

exam_day_rules.diagram_mandatory_note: Illustrate answers with labelled diagrams wherever necessary. Answer will be considered inaccurate and incomplete without a diagram.

answer_sheet_rules: question_number_note: Har answer ke upar question number AND part number (Q4a, Q4b etc.) clearly likhna zaroori hai.
set_number_note: Apna set number (348 KG / KH / KI etc.) answer sheet ke cover page par compulsory likhna hota hai.
rough_work: Answer sheet ke last page par rough work karo. ROUGH WORK clearly likho.
sequence_note: Jo aata ho pehle karo. Lekin question number clearly likho.
line_after_each_question: Har answer ke baad do lines draw karo — answers clearly separate dikhte hain.
sub_questions: Short Answer Type II questions mein (a), (b), (c), (d) parts hain. Har part ka answer clearly number karo.

pen_rules.note: Blue pen se main answer. Diagrams pencil se. Headings black pen se underline.

exam_writing_rules.rough_work_rules: Answer sheet ke last page par rough work karo. ROUGH WORK clearly likho.
exam_writing_rules.diagram_rules: Draw a neat labelled diagram wherever required. The answer will be considered inaccurate and incomplete without a diagram.
